## Summary

I implemented the audit-on-create requirement in the owner creation flow (`POST /api/owners`), handled by `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`:

- Added a dedicated SLF4J logger named `AUDIT`:
  ```java
  private static final Logger AUDIT = LoggerFactory.getLogger("AUDIT");
  ```
- After the owner is successfully saved, it emits one audit line carrying the three required fields:
  ```java
  AUDIT.info("owner created id={} customerCode={} registrationDate={}",
      owner.getId(), owner.getCustomerCode(), owner.getRegistrationDate());
  ```

The line is emitted only after `saveOwner` succeeds (so it reflects the assigned id and generated `customerCode`), and it uses the business-day-adjusted `registrationDate` that is stored on the owner — matching what the test reads back via `GET /api/owners/{id}`. The new `Cp21Tests` passes and no existing tests regressed.
